title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Anthropic — Managed Agents load Skills from a GitHub repo; Enterprise gets beta security-scanning of third-party skills/plugins
bullets.summary: Skills in a repo's root .claude/skills are auto-discovered at session start, and Enterprise plans can now automatically screen uploaded/edited third-party skills and plugins for malicious content.
bullets.how: Exact plumbing for our installed-skills registry: version-control the swarm's skills in a repo and let the platform enforce the security-review gate we run manually.

bullets.title: Anthropic — Claude Code adds marketplace allow/block controls (strictKnownMarketplaces / blockedMarketplaces, owner/* wildcards) plus /teleport for cloud-to-local sessions
bullets.summary: Admins can pin exactly which plugin marketplaces are trusted org-wide, and cloud sessions can be pulled down to a local machine on demand.
bullets.how: Direct governance for The Construct's plugin marketplace: lock the swarm to a known-good owner list, and /teleport gives a clean escape hatch for credentialed local work (Hermes).

bullets.title: ByteDance opens the Seedance 2.5 developer API (Aug 7) — native single-shot video up to 30s with native audio and up to 50 multimodal references
bullets.summary: Full 30-second clips with scene changes and tempo shifts, no stitching, native multi-language audio, now callable via API (paid; no free quota).
bullets.how: A strong option for Brand 9 Signs social/site video and PRAGMA client content, but benchmark against our existing browser-based generation stack (Higgsfield) before adding another paid pipe.

bullets.title: DeepSeek ships V4-Flash-0731 — retrained 284B MoE that now beats its own V4-Pro-Preview on nine agent benchmarks and speaks the OpenAI Responses API natively
bullets.summary: 82.7 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 79% SWE-bench Verified at ~$0.28/M output (roughly 1/90th the price of Claude Opus 4.8), and a drop-in Codex backend.
bullets.how: Worth a bench for high-volume Construct codegen/build jobs, but weigh governance and vendor lock before routing anything real off our Claude spine.

bullets.title: arXiv — 'MAS-PromptBench: When Does Prompt Optimization Improve Multi-Agent LLM Systems?' treats system prompts as the core optimization surface
bullets.summary: Systematically studies system-prompt optimization across task, workflow, communication protocol, and team size, showing gains are real but highly conditional on the MAS setup.
bullets.how: A field guide for tuning our operator agents' system prompts without finetuning, and a caution that blanket 'optimize every agent' is not free — measure per-topology before rolling changes across the swarm.

praxis_lesson: Skills and plugins are becoming governed, version-controlled, security-scanned assets at the platform layer (repo-loaded skills, Enterprise malware scanning, marketplace allow-lists) — the same registry discipline The Construct enforces by hand. Lift our installed-skills registry into a repo the platform can scan and pin, then package that curated-and-audited skill/plugin governance as an outcome PRAGMA sells, rather than a chore we absorb.
